raw.details:
Problem Statement

Ideathon

From Idea to Prototype

1. Background

As India advances toward its Vision 2047 aspirations with world-class infrastructure, smart cities, and connected transportation networks, urban mobility must evolve alongside this growth. However, challenges such as traffic congestion, poor lane discipline, unsafe driving practices, driver fatigue, distracted driving, and fragmented traffic ecosystems continue to impact road safety, travel efficiency, and the overall mobility experience.

Emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), computer vision, connected vehicle technologies, and data analytics create opportunities to develop intelligent mobility solutions that improve traffic flow, enhance road safety, and encourage responsible driving behavior.

2. The Challenge

How can emerging technologies be leveraged to develop an integrated intelligent urban mobility solution that reduces traffic congestion, improves road safety, identifies unsafe driving behaviour, enables smarter traffic management in Indian cities, and enhances the overall experience and Joy of mobility.

Participants are expected to develop innovative, technology-driven solutions addressing one or more of the following areas:

Smart Traffic Signal & Congestion Management

  • Develop IoT-based systems to monitor traffic density and identify congestion hotspots in real time.
  • Use AI to analyze traffic patterns and enable adaptive traffic signal synchronization.
  • Explore intelligent route recommendations and traffic-flow optimization.
  • Improve coordination between vehicles and traffic infrastructure.

Intelligent Lane Discipline & Violation Detection

  • Use computer vision to detect improper lane usage, unsafe lane changes, and lane departures.
  • Identify potential traffic violations and generate alerts or reports.
  • Explore corrective interventions that encourage better lane discipline.

Driver Behavior Monitoring & Fatigue Detection

  • Identify driver drowsiness, distraction, and signs of fatigue using cameras, sensors, or AI models.
  • Develop real-time driver alerts and preventive safety interventions.
  • Detect risky driving patterns such as harsh braking, rapid acceleration, speeding, and rash driving.

IoT-Based Connected Mobility Solutions

  • Develop connected systems enabling communication between vehicles, sensors, and traffic infrastructure.
  • Explore vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) and vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communication concepts.
  • Use real-time data to improve traffic awareness, hazard detection, and mobility planning.

Intelligent Safety Alerts & Corrective Interventions

  • Develop alerts for road hazards, unsafe driving conditions, and potential collision risks.
  • Design driver feedback, safety scoring, and reporting mechanisms.
  • Explore technology-enabled violation reporting and simulated penalty workflows.

Maruti Suzuki Innovation × IIT Bombay E-Summit × I Hack

Ideathon | Idea to Prototype

22 November – 12 December 2026

The Proposal | Launch applications on 22nd November, close submissions on 30th November (EOD), announce 10–15 finalist teams by 2nd December, and give selected teams a dedicated prototype-development window before the Grand Finale on 12th December 2026.

1. Strategic Rationale & Intended Outcomes

The Maruti Suzuki Innovation Team, in collaboration with IIT Bombay E-Summit, proposes IDEATHON as a student innovation challenge to source fresh, technology-enabled solutions to real-world automotive, mobility, customer-experience, manufacturing, sustainability and business-process challenges. The competition is designed around execution: selected teams will move from problem understanding to a demonstrable prototype within a focused development window.

Key Objectives:

  • Source innovative solutions from the student ecosystem that are relevant to Maruti Suzuki's business priorities.
  • Encourage practical implementation and prototype development rather than presentation-only concepts.
  • Create opportunities for interaction between students, industry experts and mentors.
  • Identify promising solutions for possible further evaluation, mentoring or pilot exploration.

Competition Architecture | Applications & Screening, Prototype Development & Grand Finale

Phase / Dates

Team Presentation Submission

Process / Milestone

What Is Assessed

01 | Applications & Screening

22–30th Nov

  • A Presentation covering problem understanding, proposed solution, intended users, technology approach.
  • Launch on Unstop and the IIT Bombay E-Summit website on 22 Nov. Applications close 30 Nov, Review on 1st–2nd Dec; announce 10–15 finalists.
  • Problem Statement relevance & user need.
  • Unique Business impact & user value.
  • Technical feasibility & scalability.
  • Viability.
  • Desirability from Mobility perspective.

02 | Prototype Development

  • Demonstrable core prototype / proof-of-concept, updated presentation, demo video or supporting material.
  • Finalists receive a focused development window. Mentoring or progress feedback may be provided subject to availability. Suggested midpoint checkpoint: 7th–8th Dec; not an elimination round.
  • Core functionality, progress against the use case, testing and learning, technical approach, business value and demonstration readiness.

03 | Grand Finale

12th Dec

  • Final pitch including live or recorded prototype demonstration, supported by relevant test evidence and an implementation roadmap.
  • Finalist teams present to the jury. Suggested format: 7-minute pitch/demo followed by 5-minute jury Q&A. Jury scoring and recognition.
  • Published final judging rubric: (prototype performance, business impact, feasibility, innovation, pitch clarity and execution).

6. Competition Timeline & Key Milestones

Date

Milestone

Key Activity

- 22nd November

  • Competition launch
  • Publish on Unstop and IIT Bombay E-Summit website; open applications.

- 22–30th November

  • Application window
  • Student registrations, team formation and solution submissions.

- 30th November, EOD

  • Application closure
  • Final deadline for application submissions (11:59 PM IST, subject to platform configuration).

- 1st and 2nd December

  • Screening & evaluation
  • Review applications against the agreed scorecard and finalize selected teams.

- TBD

  • Finalist announcement
  • Announce 10–15 selected finalist teams.

- TBD

  • Prototype development
  • Build, test and refine solutions; mentoring/progress feedback where available.

- 12th December

  • Grand Finale
  • Final pitches, prototype demonstrations, jury Q&A, evaluation and recognition.
